Tener needs que before the infinitive.

items.prompt: Mi hija tiene cuatro años y ya ___ leer.
items.explanation: A learned skill takes saber: sabe leer.
optionNotes: Tiene que means “has to”; a learned skill takes saber.
Conocer is for people and places, not skills.

items.prompt: En el museo ___ hablar en voz baja.
items.explanation: A general rule for everyone: hay que + infinitive.
optionNotes: Hay alone means “there is”; a rule needs hay que.
Tener needs que and a person: tienes que.
Deber takes the infinitive without que.

items.prompt: Tomorrow is a holiday. You tell a friend: “You don't have to come.”
items.explanation: “Don't have to” (not necessary) is no tener que.
optionNotes: No debes means “you mustn't”: it forbids.
